subject.title: [Bug]: Chrome extension browser relay removed with no cross-machine  replacement (regression)

question: Should OpenClaw restore a cross-machine Chrome extension relay, keep the relay retired, or first design a secure browser-backend Plugin SDK/API seam for optional relay-style drivers?
rationale: The requested fix would mediate authenticated browser sessions across extension, gateway, and network boundaries, and current code intentionally removed the old public config/runtime path rather than leaving a narrow broken implementation to repair.

options.title: Design a secure backend seam first
options.body: Define a versioned browser backend/driver contract, then evaluate an optional relay implementation against explicit tab scope, auth, audit, packaging, migration, and docs requirements.

options.title: Keep the relay retired
options.body: Leave `driver: "extension"` unsupported and improve migration guidance toward node host, remote CDP, and external tools for users who can accept those tradeoffs.

options.title: Restore a first-party relay directly
options.body: Reintroduce the old extension relay as an opt-in first-party driver, accepting the larger security and compatibility review burden in core.

recommendation.title: Design a secure backend seam first
recommendation.body: Define a versioned browser backend/driver contract, then evaluate an optional relay implementation against explicit tab scope, auth, audit, packaging, migration, and docs requirements.

likelyOwner.reason: vincentkoc owns the strongest recent history on the browser driver migration and profile-driver seam that removed this path.
